# Ashlr MD

> Open-source Markdown app for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Agents install one command, call a CLI that prints JSON, and drive the live document over MCP.

This file is the agent manual. The same commands live in the README and in docs/EXAMPLES.md. The exhaustive per-tool notes live in docs/AGENTS.md. Tool order comes from `tool_registry()` in `src-tauri/bins/mdopener-mcp/src/lib.rs`.

## What it is

Ashlr MD renders Markdown on macOS, Windows, and Linux. `mdopen` opens a file in the app. `mdopener-mcp` is the MCP server agents launch over stdio. `open_file` is the only tool that starts the app. The server talks to the app on `127.0.0.1` with a token in `~/.mdopener/`.

People use the window to read, edit, and export. Agents use the CLI and the MCP tools.

## Install

macOS or Linux, from a checkout. Needs git, curl, Rust (Cargo), and Bun; the script stops and names the first one missing. This builds the CLI and the MCP server and skips the desktop app.

```bash
SKIP_APP_BUILD=1 bash scripts/install.sh
```

No checkout:

```bash
SKIP_APP_BUILD=1 bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/main/scripts/install.sh)
```

Run this way, the script clones into `~/ashlr-md` (set `CLONE_DIR` to change it), or fast-forwards that clone when it exists. The current directory does not matter.

The script links `mdopen` and `mdopener-mcp` into `/usr/local/bin`, or into `~/.local/bin` when that directory is not writable. If the commands are missing:

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

When `claude` is on `PATH`, the script registers the MCP server. The desktop app is a release download: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md

Windows uses the NSIS installer, then the PowerShell commands in docs/EXAMPLES.md. The bash script is not the Windows install.

## JSON commands

These exit without reading MCP stdin. `doctor` and `setup --local` do not download a model and do not write config.

```bash
mdopener-mcp --version
mdopener-mcp doctor --json
mdopener-mcp doctor --fix --json
mdopener-mcp setup --local --json
mdopener-mcp --ashlr-handshake --json
mdopener-mcp --export-tool-schema
```

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `doctor --json` | one JSON object, `"kind": "ashlr.doctor"` |
| `doctor --fix --json` | one JSON object, `"kind": "ashlr.doctor"`, with `mode`, `plan`, and `outcome`. Dry run. Writes nothing |
| `doctor --fix --apply --json` | the same shape, and it makes the repairs |
| `setup --local --json` | one JSON object, `"kind": "ashlr.setup-local"`, `downloads` false, `writes` false |
| `--ashlr-handshake --json` | one JSON object, `"kind": "ashlr.handshake"` |
| `--export-tool-schema` | tool names and input schemas as JSON, sorted by name |
| `--version --json`, `--help --json`, `--export-tool-schema --json` | one JSON object with a `kind` of `ashlr.version`, `ashlr.help`, or `ashlr.tool-schema`, `schema_version: 1`, and `tool: "ashlr-md"` |

`--json` may come before or after the flag, and `-V` and `-h` work too. Check `kind` and `schema_version`, and allow extra fields in version 1.

`doctor` and `setup --local` exit 0 whatever they find, so read the JSON, not the exit code. Fields: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/local-ai.md#json-output

`mdopener-mcp doctor --apply` without `--fix` exits 2 and writes nothing. Repair rules: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/doctor-fix.md

## Connect MCP

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user ashlr-md "$(command -v mdopener-mcp)"
codex mcp add ashlr-md -- "$(command -v mdopener-mcp)"
python3 scripts/connect-cursor.py
```

Restart Claude Code after the first command. Codex picks the server up on its next run. The Cursor script merges `ashlr-md` into `~/.cursor/mcp.json` and writes nothing if that file is not JSON, if `mcpServers` is not an object, or if `ashlr-md` already points at a different program that still exists. Reload MCP in Cursor Settings.

In the desktop app: Preferences, AI agents (MCP), then Connect to Claude Code, Connect to Cursor, or Connect to Codex.

## Open a file

```bash
mdopen samples/agent-plan.md
mdopen --edit samples/agent-plan.md
echo '# Hello' | mdopen -
```

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--edit`, `-e` | open in edit mode |
| `--read`, `-r` | open in read mode, the default; not with `--edit` |
| `-` | read Markdown from stdin (up to 16 MiB) and open it from a temp file |
| `--` | end of flags, for a file whose name starts with a dash |
| `--hook` | Claude Code PostToolUse hook; reads the hook JSON on stdin |
| `--help`, `-h` / `--version`, `-V` | help or version |

`mdopen` exits 0 when the running app accepted the file, or when the app was not running and the `mdopener://` URL was handed to the OS launcher (if the launcher is still running after 10 s, it prints a note and the open is not confirmed). It exits 1 on bad usage, a missing, directory or non-Markdown path (`.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdown`, `.mkd`, `.mdx`, no dotfiles), empty stdin for `-`, a failed launcher, or when the running app refused the file or did not answer within 6 s; stderr says which. `mdopen --hook` exits 0 and prints nothing (another argument with it is bad usage, exit 1); it opens only the Markdown file that a successful Write, Edit or MultiEdit names. Preferences, AI agents (MCP), Auto-open agent Markdown adds that hook to `~/.claude/settings.json`. Rules: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md#auto-open-hook

The window requires the desktop app. The JSON commands above do not.

Deep link, when the app is installed:

```text
mdopener://open?path=/absolute/path/to/file.md
mdopener://open?path=/absolute/path/to/file.md&mode=edit
```

## Tools

`mdopener-mcp --export-tool-schema` is the source for arguments. Order in `tools/list`:

<!-- doclive: seq src-tauri/bins/mdopener-mcp/src/lib.rs#tool_registry /^\s+name: "([a-z_]+)",$/ vs /^\d+\. `([a-z_]+)`/ -->

1. `open_file` starts the app. `path` is required. `mode` is `read` or `edit`.
2. `get_current_content` returns the open document. Error when none is open.
3. `list_recent` lists recent files. The app must already be running.
4. `request_review` blocks for a human verdict. Pass `path` or `content`, or a `review_id` to keep waiting.
5. `get_user_annotations` reads the latest verdict and task checkboxes. Works from disk when the app is closed.
6. `edit_document` replaces one exact `find` with `replace`. `save` defaults to false.
7. `search_vault` searches the watched folder and recents. When the app is closed, `vault` names a directory to search on disk instead.
8. `present_document` switches the open doc to a distraction-free read view. It does not start the app.
9. `list_ai_actions` lists editor AI actions. No app required.
10. `get_conversation_context` reads a saved chat session. No app required.
11. `save_conversation_message` appends one message to that session. No app required.
12. `diff_documents` diffs two Markdown files on disk. No app required.
13. `stream_edit` previews a find/replace as a diff.
14. `stream_edit_apply` applies a preview.
15. `export_text` returns plain text with Markdown syntax stripped. With `path` it reads that file from disk, no app required.
16. `export_metadata` returns headings, front matter, and wikilinks. With `path` it reads that file from disk, no app required.
17. `edit_canvas` edits a `.canvas` file. It writes by default. No app required.
18. `export` exports the open document. Formats: `pdf`, `docx`, `html`, `epub`. With `output_path` the document must be in Read view. PDF takes no `output_path`.
19. `replace_document` replaces the whole open document.
20. `set_content` is the same whole-document replace.

Prefer `edit_document` over `set_content` and `replace_document`.

The other tools act on the window and need the running app. `open_file` starts it; no other tool does. Details: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md#how-it-works-the-ipc-model

`open_file` arguments:

```json
{"path": "samples/agent-plan.md", "mode": "read"}
```

`edit_document` arguments. `find` must occur once:

```json
{"find": "## Phase 1: Core", "replace": "## Phase 1: Foundation", "path": "samples/agent-plan.md", "save": false}
```

`request_review` arguments:

```json
{"path": "samples/agent-plan.md", "blocking": true}
```

A blocking call returns `verdict` of `approved`, `changes_requested`, `dismissed`, `timeout`, or `superseded`, or `status` `pending` with a `reviewId` when the wait ends first. Call `request_review` again with that `review_id` to keep waiting.

`export` arguments. HTML, DOCX, and EPUB can take `output_path` in an existing directory; the app then writes the file without a dialog, which needs Read view, so call `open_file` with `"mode": "read"` first. Without `output_path` the app opens its export dialog. PDF always opens the system print dialog. An existing file is replaced only with `"overwrite": true`.

```json
{"format": "html", "output_path": "/tmp/agent-plan.html", "overwrite": false}
```

Prompts you can hand an agent:

```text
Open samples/agent-plan.md in Ashlr MD with open_file, then show get_current_content.
```

```text
Call edit_document on the open document. find must match once. Then request_review and wait for my verdict.
```

## Resources

The server also answers `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list`, and `resources/read`. Order in `resources/list`:

<!-- doclive: seq src-tauri/bins/mdopener-mcp/src/lib.rs#handle_resources_list /^ {8}"uri": "([^"]+)",$/ vs /^- `([a-z]+:\/\/[a-z-]+)`/ -->

- `mdopener://current` is the open document as Markdown. Error `-32002` when none is open, `-32000` when the app is not running.
- `text://vault-search` is `search_vault` as a resource. Read `text://vault-search?q=<query>`, with optional `&limit=` (1 to 200), `&vault=<directory>`, and `&semantic=false` or `true`. Without `&vault=` it needs the running app. It is also the one template in `resources/templates/list`.
- `mdopener://recent-documents` lists recent files that still exist, each with `path`, `title`, `mtimeMs`, and a 200-character `preview`.
- `file://<path>` entries follow, one per Markdown file in the app's watched folder. `resources/read` reads only paths the app lists in the vault or recents. Open any other file with `open_file` first.

## Prompts

`prompts/list` and `prompts/get` serve three prompts. Each returns one `user` message: the instruction, then the open document. None takes arguments. With no document open, `prompts/get` returns `-32002`.

<!-- doclive: seq src-tauri/bins/mdopener-mcp/src/lib.rs#prompts_list /^\s+\{ "name": "([a-z_]+)", "description": described\(/ vs /^- `([a-z_]+)`/ -->

- `summarize` asks for the document's key points as a short bulleted list.
- `review_plan` reviews the document as a plan and flags risks, gaps, and unclear steps.
- `improve_writing` tightens the prose without changing its meaning.

Full rules: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md#resources-reference

## Local AI

Nothing is sent to a cloud model unless the person opts in.

- macOS 26 or later on Apple Silicon: Apple Foundation Models, after Apple Intelligence is on. No API key.
- Other machines: Ollama, or a `localInference` block in `~/.ashlr/config.json`.
- `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` defaults to `https://api.anthropic.com`. `https://` to any host is accepted. Plain `http://` is accepted only for `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`. Refusals send no request and do not repeat the value.
- `OLLAMA_HOST` for the app defaults to `http://localhost:11434`. A remote host needs `localInference.allowRemote: true` and `https://`. The environment cannot allow a remote host by itself.
- The MCP sidecar's default, when `OLLAMA_HOST` is unset, is `http://127.0.0.1:11434`. It refuses `http://localhost`.
- The default local model name is `qwen3.8:27b`. Names containing `abliterat` or `uncensored` are refused. No API key is sent to a `localInference` URL.
- `"offline": true` on that block refuses cloud calls, including through a loopback gateway.

Full rules: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/local-ai.md

```bash
mdopener-mcp doctor --json
mdopener-mcp setup --local --json
```

## Phantom

Phantom calls `mdopen` for `phm inbox show <id> --open` and `phm digest --open` when Ashlr MD is installed. The URL scheme is `mdopener://`. Under `phantom exec -- <cmd>`, keys arrive as `phm_` placeholders. Set `ASHLR_MD_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FROM_ENV=1` to read `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the environment. A `phm_` placeholder is honored only when the base URL is the session proxy.

Contract: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/PHANTOM.md

## Security, short

The IPC server binds to `127.0.0.1`. The token file is `~/.mdopener/ipc-token`. Tools that take a path open Markdown documents that are not dotfiles. `mdopener-mcp doctor --fix` never changes `ipc-token`. Run `chmod 600 ~/.mdopener/ipc-token` yourself when doctor says to.

Threat model: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/SECURITY.md

## Part of Ashlr

Phantom and its ecosystem form a fully autonomous, code-first, agent-native software factory. Agents run it; the human is a passive board member. The goal is open source RSI (recursive self improvement): agents that keep improving the tools they work with, these repositories included.

Ashlr MD is the factory's Markdown surface: where an agent hands a document to a person, and where an agent opens, edits, exports, and waits for approval over MCP. Each tool installs on its own.

| Tool | Command | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Phantom (https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom) | `phm` | agent workbench |
| Phantom Secrets (https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom-secrets) | `phantom` | `phm_` placeholders for API keys |
| Locus (https://github.com/ashlrai/locus) | `locus` | one account per agent session |
| Lexicon (https://lexicon.ashlr.ai) | `lexicon` | dictation corrections |
| Ashlr Stack (https://stack.ashlr.ai) | `stack` | service provisioning |
| ashlr-plugin (https://plugin.ashlr.ai/) | `ashlr-plugin` | token-efficiency tools |

Agents maintain this repository. Phantom (`phm improve`) and other coding agents open pull requests, merge them once the required checks pass, and fix `main` forward. Rules: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/AGENTS.md. Checks: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

To contribute, as a person or with a coding agent: fork the repository, branch from `main`, run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` (it installs what `bun.lock` pins, as CI does), make one small change, then run `scripts/ci-local.sh upstream/main` (it always runs typecheck, Biome, the crypto policy, version sync, doc links and the conflict and selector tests, and uses `scripts/ci/select.mjs` to add Vitest on changed files and `cargo clippy` plus `cargo test` on affected crates when the diff needs them). It does not run the two diff secret scans (Gitleaks and the secret-shape scan), which both block the required check; the walkthrough shows how to run them locally. It also skips five steps of the required check's fast job: `bun run test:unit` (its punctuation test fails on an em or en dash, even in Markdown docs), the CI gate regression tests, the dependency plan parser tests, the npm script path test and `bun run check:workflow-bash`; the walkthrough lists the commands. Many docs double as test fixtures: a test checks their examples, headings, counts or lists against the code, and no pull request job runs those tests on a docs-only diff. After editing `README.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `llms.txt`, the landing page or a guide in `docs/`, run the test that reads it (`src/docFacts.test.ts` reads most of them, via `bunx vitest run --project unit src/docFacts.test.ts`); the walkthrough has the full table. Push to your fork and open a pull request against `main`. `Check (Linux)` is the one required check; once it is green the pull request merges through auto-merge and the merge queue. On a fork pull request a maintainer or fleet agent arms auto-merge. Walkthrough: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contribute-with-an-agent
